subject: psychiatry
title: Other psychotic disorders

steps.tx: Psychotic disorders separate mainly by **duration, symptom breadth and mood overlap**. Brief psychotic disorder erupts suddenly with delusions, hallucinations or disorganisation lasting days to under one month with full return to baseline, often after marked stress. Schizophreniform disorder looks identical to schizophrenia but runs one to six months, reserving schizophrenia label for longer courses.
steps.say: Days of psychosis recovering fully is brief disorder. One to six months schizophrenia like is schizophreniform.

steps.tx: **Delusional disorder** sustains one or more delusions for at least a month with otherwise near normal functioning, minimal hallucinations (if present, tied to delusional theme) and no prior schizophrenia picture. Themes include erotomanic (another loves them), grandiose, jealous (Othello), persecutory and somatic (Ekbom infestation). Behaviour is rational outside the delusional system, making engagement and risk assessment (jealousy violence, stalking in erotomania) central.
steps.say: One encapsulated delusion, life otherwise intact: delusional disorder. Jealous and erotomanic types carry risk to others.

steps.tx: **Schizoaffective disorder** requires a major mood episode concurrent with active psychosis for most of illness, plus at least two weeks of delusions or hallucinations without mood symptoms, proving psychosis independence. It splits bipolar and depressive types. Diagnostic reliability is low and longitudinal review often revises it toward schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, so timelines from collateral sources decide more than cross sectional impressions.
steps.say: Mood plus psychosis most of time, but psychosis alone for two weeks: schizoaffective. Timelines overrule snapshots.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Secondary psychoses must always be excluded: substances (stimulants, cannabis, steroids, withdrawal), delirium, dementia, temporal lobe epilepsy, autoimmune encephalitis (anti NMDA receptor with ovarian teratoma in young women), thyroid and other endocrine disease, and postpartum psychosis which is usually bipolar spectrum emergency. New psychosis after 40, visual hallucinations, confusion or neurological signs demand medical workup before primary psychiatric labelling.
steps.say: Late, visual, confused or neurological psychosis is medical until disproven. Postpartum psychosis is an emergency.
